record_type_quote: This study examined response times and accuracy in short-term JOR tasks. We replicated and extended classic results from the short-term JOR task.

targets.title: Speed and accuracy of recency judgments for events in short-term memory.
targets.evidence_quote: The classic ﬁnding from short-term relative JOR tasks is that correct response time (RT) depends on the lag to the more recent item but not to the less recent item (see Fig. 1, Muter, 1979; Hacker, 1980; Hockley, 1984).
targets.outcome_quote: This study replicated the classical ﬁnding in a relative JOR task that correct RT depends on the lag to the more recent probe but not on the lag to the less recent probe (Fig. 2b).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The paper explicitly replicates the classic correct-RT finding attributed jointly to these papers and confirms it in the discussion.

reasoning: New sample tests the classic short-term JOR finding attributed to Muter, Hacker and Hockley; closely follows Hacker Experiment 2. McElree and Dosher is cited for the explanatory scanning model, not explicitly for the finding being replicated. Howard et al. motivates a new extension; longer-timescale and strategic-control studies are contextual rather than targets.
